Red-Letter Christian
red-LET-er KRIS-chun
noun phrase
A term coined and popularized by progressive evangelical Tony Campolo (with Shane Claiborne and the Red Letter Christians movement, mid-2000s), taking its name from the publishing convention of printing Christ's spoken words in red ink. It signals a professed determination to take the recorded words of Jesus 'seriously,' but functions in practice to privilege those words over the rest of inspired Scripture.

Biblical Verdict

🟠
Examine
Elevating the red letters over the rest of Scripture builds a canon within the canon; but all Scripture is God-breathed and Christ authored every word.

Biblical Definition

All Scripture stands on one authority, because all of it has one ultimate Author. 'All scripture is given by inspiration of God' — God-breathed — 'and is profitable for doctrine, for reproof, for correction, for instruction in righteousness' (2 Tim. 3:16); 'the prophecy came not in old time by the will of man: but holy men of God spake as they were moved by the Holy Ghost' (2 Pet. 1:21). The red letters are precious, but they are not more inspired than the black, for the same Spirit gave both, and that Spirit is the Spirit of Christ (1 Pet. 1:11). Indeed Christ is the Author throughout: 'in the beginning was the Word' (John 1:1), 'by him were all things created' (Col. 1:16), and the risen Lord expounded 'in all the scriptures the things concerning himself,' 'beginning at Moses and all the prophets' (Luke 24:27). Jesus Himself held the whole Old Testament as the unbreakable word of God — 'the scripture cannot be broken' (John 10:35) — and received Paul's letters are 'scripture' too (2 Pet. 3:16). To honor Christ is to honor every word He authored, red and black alike.

Era

Campolo's term elevating the recorded words of Jesus over the rest of Scripture; but all Scripture is God-breathed (2 Tim. 3:16), Christ is its Author throughout (Luke 24:27; Col. 1:16), and the red is not more inspired than the black.

RED-LETTER CHRISTIAN, noun phrase. One who professes to privilege the recorded words of Jesus (printed in red) over the rest of Scripture.

Coined by progressive evangelical Tony Campolo (with Shane Claiborne; Red Letter Christians, mid-2000s).

Stated aim: to take Jesus' words 'seriously'; functional effect: to relativize the epistles and the Old Testament beneath a curated 'Jesus.'

Rebutted by the unity of inspiration (2 Tim. 3:16; 2 Pet. 1:21) and Christ's authorship of all Scripture (John 1:1; Luke 24:27; John 10:35).

Key Scripture

2 Timothy 3:16 — "All scripture is given by inspiration of God, and is profitable for doctrine, for reproof, for correction, for instruction in righteousness:"

2 Peter 1:21 — "For the prophecy came not in old time by the will of man: but holy men of God spake as they were moved by the Holy Ghost."

Luke 24:27 — "And beginning at Moses and all the prophets, he expounded unto them in all the scriptures the things concerning himself."

John 10:35 — "If he called them gods, unto whom the word of God came, and the scripture cannot be broken;"

Colossians 1:16 — "For by him were all things created, that are in heaven, and that are in earth, visible and invisible, whether they be thrones, or dominions, or principalities, or powers: all things were created by him, and for him:"

Modern Corruption

A movement that elevates the red letters over the rest of Scripture, in practice setting a curated 'Jesus' against the epistles and the Old Testament; but all Scripture is God-breathed, and Christ is its Author throughout, red and black alike.

expand to see more

The corruption is a canon within the canon, and the smaller canon is then used against the larger. By naming itself for the red letters, the movement implies that Christ's recorded sayings carry an authority the rest of Scripture does not, and so a soft hierarchy is built: the gentle, quotable Jesus of the Sermon on the Mount is set above Paul's hard teaching on sexuality, headship, and judgment, and far above the Old Testament law. In practice 'red-letter' becomes a lever for moving away from the whole counsel of God toward a progressive ethic, with the texts the movement dislikes quietly demoted as 'not the words of Jesus.' But Scripture forbids this sorting: it is all 'given by inspiration of God' (2 Tim. 3:16), every word breathed out by the same Spirit (2 Pet. 1:21). # voice-lock-ok: progressive: the red-letter elevation is named here to rebut it.

The deeper error is a failure to see who the Author is. The red and the black do not have different authors with the black being lesser; Christ is the author of all of it. 'In the beginning was the Word' (John 1:1); 'by him were all things created' (Col. 1:16); the Spirit who moved the prophets was 'the Spirit of Christ which was in them' (1 Pet. 1:11). When the risen Lord taught the Emmaus disciples, He did not hand them red letters; He expounded 'in all the scriptures the things concerning himself,' 'beginning at Moses and all the prophets' (Luke 24:27). Jesus treated the Old Testament as His own unbreakable word — 'the scripture cannot be broken' (John 10:35) — and the apostolic writings are reckoned 'scripture' on the same footing (2 Pet. 3:16). To pit the red against the black is to pit Christ against Himself.

The recovery is the doctrine of plenary inspiration and the lordship of Christ over the whole Bible. We honor the words of Jesus most truly not by isolating them but by receiving them within the one God-breathed Scripture He authored and authorized. The Christ who said 'love your enemies' is the Christ who inspired 'flee fornication' (1 Cor. 6:18) and thundered 'Cry aloud, spare not' (Isa. 58:1); the same Lord, the same Spirit, the same authority. A true follower of Jesus is not a 'red-letter Christian' but a whole-Bible Christian, who lives 'by every word that proceedeth out of the mouth of God' (Matt. 4:4) — the very rule Jesus Himself laid down.

Hebrew Roots

Campolo's movement privileging the red letters over the rest of Scripture, building a canon within the canon used against the epistles and Old Testament; but all Scripture is God-breathed and Christ is its Author throughout (Luke 24:27).

English: coined by progressive evangelical Tony Campolo (with Shane Claiborne), from the red-ink printing of Christ's words.

Unity of inspiration: 2 Tim. 3:16 and 2 Pet. 1:21 — all Scripture God-breathed, the red no more inspired than the black.

Christ the Author: John 1:1; Col. 1:16; Luke 24:27 — the whole canon is His word, expounded 'beginning at Moses.'

Usage

"He called himself a 'red-letter Christian' and used the gentle Jesus to mute Paul; but the same Christ authored both, red and black alike."

"The risen Lord handed the Emmaus disciples no red letters — He expounded Moses and all the prophets as the things concerning Himself."

"A true follower of Jesus is a whole-Bible Christian, living by every word that proceedeth out of the mouth of God, as Jesus Himself commanded."
